did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with a declaration of trust: the psalmist says that the Lord is his refuge and asks that he never be put to shame.
The psalmist uses three images of protection—a rock, a dwelling place, and a fortress—to describe the Lord as a constant refuge.
The psalmist describes the Lord as his hope and trust since his youth, emphasizing that faith has accompanied him throughout his life.

The psalmist presents his relationship with the Lord as beginning at birth: he says that he has relied on Him from the womb and that, ever since leaving his mother’s womb, the Lord has been his source of life and protection.
The psalmist says that he has become an example to many, but notes that the Lord is his strong refuge; in this way, his personal situation becomes a testimony to the power of divine protection.
The psalmist’s request not to be cast away in old age or abandoned when his strength is gone expresses the need for divine support at every stage of life.
The enemies do more than threaten the psalmist: they consult together and act against him. This emphasizes that the danger is an organized persecution.
Despite the threats, the psalmist declares that he will continue to hope in the Lord and add to all His praise. Hope and praise are presented as his response to danger.
The psalmist says that the Lord has taught him since his youth, and he continues to proclaim His wonders to this day. The verse connects learning, personal experience, and testimony.
After describing many troubles, the psalmist asks the Lord to revive him, raise him up from the depths of the earth, and restore life and hope to him.
Praise in the chapter also takes musical form: the psalmist mentions the harp and lyre and describes the Lord as the God of truth and the Holy One of Israel.

The chapter ends with continued praise of the Lord’s righteousness and the hope that those seeking the psalmist’s harm will be put to shame and disgraced. The conclusion returns to the themes of justice and salvation.
